predecessors.name: Kingdom of Germany
predecessors.text: Alamannia: Baden-Württemberg and the Augsburg country, Alsace west of the Rhine, and Switzerland east of the Reuss; 'from the Vosges in the west to the Lech in the east, and south to Chiavenna and…

successors.name: House of Hohenstaufen
successors.text: Cliopatria's single Hohenstaufen shape, 1260-1271: Swabia from Alsace to Lake Constance, about 50,800 km2 (gazetteer figures: 53,000 km2)

ledger.x: 915: Erchanger proclaims himself duke of Swabia.
917: Burchard II becomes duke after Erchanger's execution.
919: King Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy seizes the county of Zürich.
919: Burchard II defeats Rudolph II at Winterthur and Rudolph leaves Zürich.
948: Hermann I dies and Otto the Great gives the duchy to his son Liudolf; the Ottonian house takes Swabia.
1038: Hermann IV dies and Henry (later Henry III) receives the duchy; the duchy is in the royal house's hands until 1045.
1096: Frederick I cedes the Breisgau to Berthold II of Zähringen, the rival duke of 1092; in 1098 Berthold 'reconciled with Frederick, renounced all claims to Swabia' and became Duke of Zähringen.
1198: the Ortenau goes to the Zähringer (soft).
1260: the dossier hands the duchy to house-of-hohenstaufen.

wars.name: Conrad I's war against Erchanger and Burchard
wars.outcome: Erchanger and Burchard II defeated Conrad I at Wahlwies in 915; Erchanger was executed on Conrad's order on 21 January 917 and Burchard II became duke.

wars.name: Battle of Winterthur
wars.outcome: Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy seized the county of Zürich in 919 and was defeated by Burchard II at Winterthur; peace was affirmed in 922.

wars.name: Zähringen contest for Swabia
wars.outcome: Berthold II was elected duke of Swabia in 1092 against Frederick I; in 1096 Frederick ceded the Breisgau and in 1098 Berthold renounced Swabia and became Duke of Zähringen.

certainty.note: Stem-duchy frontiers (the Vosges, the Lech, the Gotthard) are descriptive; no treaty fixes them on the pages opened.
